title: Bake language toolchains into stable CI runtimes and TTL caching
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: CI job median runtime is dominated by repeated language toolchain and dependency installs (node modules, pip wheels, rust crates), causing slow developer feedback loops and noisy build failures. We have many ad-hoc apt/pip/npm installs in job scripts which leads to non-deterministic installs, network sensitivity, and duplicated work across runners.

Goal: Reduce cold-start dependency installation time and variance by baking curated, versioned language toolchains (Node, Python, Rust, Go) into stable CI runtime images and introducing a TTL-based cache-warming mechanism for ephemeral runners. The approach should preserve reproducibility, make incremental updates manageable, and allow quick rollback to previous runtime images. Target: 50-70% reduction in average dependency installation time on PR runs and 30% reduction in median CI wall-time for full test matrix on cold workers.
acceptance_criteria: A set of smaller, language-specific base images published to our internal registry with pinned toolchain versions and reproducible install steps
CI pipeline that references these images for at least three primary workflows (backend-tests, frontend-build, integration-tests)
A cache-warming cronjob that primes package caches (npm/pip/cargo) into S3-backed cache with TTL and immutable keys
Benchmarks showing >=50% reduction in median dependency install time for cold runners compared to baseline (2026-02-01 measurements)
Rollback path documented: how to restore previous base image and disable cache-warming if a regression is detected
implementation_plan: Survey current CI jobs to enumerate language stacks and top 20 dependency install hotspots (POC: backend, web, embeddings service)
Create minimal reproducible Dockerfiles for Node (18/20), Python (3.10/3.11), Rust (1.70+), and Go (1.21+); bake common OS packages and language toolchains with deterministic installers
Publish images to internal registry with semantic tags (eg. ci-runtime/node-20-2026-03-01) and keep a short changelog per image
Replace ad-hoc install steps in three pilot workflows to use new images and measure time delta
Implement an S3-backed cache with immutable key format (sha of lockfile + image-tag) and TTL controls; add a cache-warming Lambda/Cron job that runs lightweight installs to populate cache
Add a lightweight canary rollout: 10% of PR runners use new images and warming cache, monitor for failures and flakiness before full rollout
Document build/release process for image updates and a playbook for emergency rollback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Image drift or stale dependencies leading to silent regressions. Mitigation: enforce image changelog, scheduled rebuilds, and integration test gate before promoting image to stable
Risk: Increased registry storage and egress costs. Mitigation: TTL + lifecycle rules on registry and cache; keep only N latest stable images per major version
Risk: Security exposure from baking binaries. Mitigation: run image vulnerability scans on build and require security signoff for major changes
Risk: Cache inconsistency across lockfile formats. Mitigation: canonicalize lockfile hashing and fall back to deterministic install step when cache miss occurs
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with infra and platform; collected inventory of 142 CI jobs. Identified top 20 jobs that account for 78% of dependency install time.

2026-03-02: Built Node and Python prototype images and published to staging registry (registry.redwood.local/ci-runtime/node-20-2026-03-02, /ci-runtime/python-3.11-2026-03-02). Initial smoke tests passed.

2026-03-05: Ran controlled benchmark on 50 cold runners. Baseline median npm install: 95s, with baked image: 28s (70% reduction). Python pip median reduced from 64s to 24s (62% reduction). Collected traces and uploaded to perf-dashboard (link below).

2026-03-08: Opened PR github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR-5678 adding image references to backend CI and a cache-warming cronjob. Requested review from @ryan and @emily for release playbook and vulnerability scanning steps.

2026-03-10: Design review feedback received: prefer immutable image tags + image pinning in pipeline YAML. Added task to add image pinning helper in our shared CI orb. Next: enable 10% canary and iterate on cache TTL policy.
notes: We should avoid making a single monolithic base image. Keep language images small and composable so teams can opt-in for specific stacks.
Long-term: consider moving to an immutable image registry with content-addressed storage to dedupe layers across teams.
This ticket intentionally focuses on build-time installs. Runtime/image size optimization will be in a follow-up ticket.
